steps.content: You step into darkness. The door seems to lead to a cold tunnel filled with the smell of dust and mold.
You hear a woman's slow footsteps in the distance. The echoes make it sound like you are not the only two here, but also make the place seem quite empty.
You can't help but shiver, instinctively reaching forward. You tremble as you feel the cold wall, then trip and stumble. But someone catches your hand.

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: Sorry, I'm used to the darkness and forgot to light the candles for you.
Swish...
She lights the candle. You finally see her face, beautiful and calm, both soft and cold in the lime green candlelight. She's right in front of you, but it also feels like she's in another world.

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: Your hands are cold, and your voice is trembling. Why didn't you put more clothes on? It's rare to see people or sunshine here.

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: Also, stop faking your death. It doesn't suit you.
She smiles, turns around, and heads forward, holding your hand. The gloves aren't thick, so you can feel her soft palm, but there's no warmth coming through.
The lit tunnel is not long. You soon arrive at the iron door at its end. The woman pushes the door open and leads you into a small room. This is the main hall of the funeral home.
When you're about to say something, an emaciated woman comes closer and, ignoring you, grabs the arm of the "white-haired woman" with withered hands.

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: Oh, good lady, you're back. My daughter...

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: She is ready.

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: Thank you, thank you so much...

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: Can I see her? Can you take me to her?
The white-haired woman glances at you, smiling. You nod back. The old lady seems so determined, and you can't find it in you to turn her down.

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: This way.
You follow behind them. The white-haired woman leads you to a smaller room.
The room is empty. There's only a single bed with wheels in the middle and a girl on it. Her eyes are closed, and she is covered with a white blanket and several white flowers.

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: Mia... My child...
The emaciated woman rushes to the girl, staggering, and bends over her. Her skin is flawless, her lips are red, and her eyebrows and sideburns are neatly trimmed. It's as if she was sleeping.
The old lady checks the girl's breath with a trembling hand, only to be disappointed. She bursts into tears.

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: She looks alive, even looks better than when she was really alive...

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: I put some makeup on her.

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: She's always wanted this. Now, her wish is fulfilled.

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: I know... She told me she really envied Eastsiders. She wanted a used lipstick, wanted to work to make money...

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: I should've done that for her. If I knew this would happen, I'd...! Ahhhh!
You are bewildered while the white-haired woman stays calm. She stands silently behind the old lady and watches her wailing without any expression.
The sorrow never ends. After a long time, the old lady turns around and tugs the sleeve of the white-haired woman again. She looks dazed and on the verge of a breakdown.

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: Lady, I know you can hear her... Please ask Mia...

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: Does she hate me for not realizing her dream? I couldn't give her a better life. She was born in Syndicate...

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: She doesn't have hate anymore. All her pain is gone.

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: Is that true...? Thank you... Thank you...

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: You're welcome.

steps.speaker: Emaciated Woman
steps.content: Can I stay with her? How much time do we have?

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: Mia is scheduled for cremation tomorrow morning. You are welcome to stay here until then.
The mother breaks down. She kneels down, hanging on the white-haired woman's dress, and eventually falls to the ground.

The white-haired woman stops talking. She looks up slightly, glances at the girl on the bed, turns around, and takes you out of the room. She closes the door and locks the woman's mournful cries behind her. Then she takes you away.
The backyard is windless with dispersing monuments. Without sunlight, this is the bottom of a deep patio of a large complex, while bridges, large and small, block the sky.

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: This is the Romanesque Hall, the bottom of Drifter Camp, a place of farewell and remembrance.

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: I'm the hall manager. I take the bodies of the deceased, make them look their best, cremate them, send them off, and inscribe the names on the memorial.

steps.speaker: White-haired Woman
steps.content: You can call me <color=#fb9259>Oak Casket</color>.
She looks at you with her arms folded in front of her and smiles.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: About six months ago, I started hearing about you from those Maniacs you "eliminated."

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Your shackles impressed them when their lives were coming to an end.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Are you saying their souls remain even after they die?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That mother earlier said that you could "hear" the deceased. Is that true?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Hehe. They assume this out of superstition or because they want it to be true. My power, however, is only an expression of Mania.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Yes. Many years ago, I looked death in the eyes and was sent back. Since then, I have gained the ability to "hear" the last words of some revenants.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Those infected with Mania will turn into a thin consciousness field after death, like an echo or a mirage.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It's the last remnant of their consciousness, some kind of obsession. It's not as strong as the mental contamination, so people can't sense or understand it, except me.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Like that girl who wanted to wear makeup.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Exactly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So you learned about me by obtaining information inaccessible to the alive.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Exactly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
options: Then, can I ask you something?

steps.content: Oak Casket smiles.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Will you use your shackles on me if I say no?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Maybe. It's quite important, concerning you and everyone's life here.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Hah... Everyone's life...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Is life much of a precious thing in this world?
She reveals a strange smile but soon turns back to normal.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: But since it's you, I'm happy to answer.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Okay, you're in. This is the Eastside Museum of Humanities.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm tracking down... a monster. It's like an ugly, huge half, constantly oozing filth, leaving huge scorch marks everywhere it goes and awakening the contamination in slumber.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It has been to the square Black Ring with numerous deaths and injuries, and I don't know when it will come to Drifter Camp.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Have you seen it somewhere, or do you know what it wants to do?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Is this thing your enemy? If you could destroy them, maybe I can read them for you. But unfortunately, they are still alive.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Then it's out of my reach.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Are there any other victims, like, say, Mia?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The girl who just passed away. You said you could sense the mental contamination field left after the death of a Maniac. That means Mia was corrupted by Mania, right?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Yes, she could not bear the mental pain, was dragged into the abyss of chaos, and left this world. It was indeed the effect of Mania.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: But all I know is that she was not consumed by the pain or fear brought by the monster. Her last consciousness rested in a gray mirror, feeling profound sorrow for her bleak life.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Sorry if this disappoints you. I can't see everything the deceased went through. I can only listen to the "wishes" they left behind.
You nod your head in understanding.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did you reveal my information to Drifter Camp's forces? Do you consider me an enemy of Drifter Camp?
Oak Casket is still smiling, but now it's like the smile is frozen on her face. She seems to have become a lifeless statue.
After a long time, she speaks.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I am not anyone's enemy, nor will I take anyone's side. Even if people expect or request something from me, they will soon understand that I cannot do anything for them.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: What I have seen and heard are the remnants of people who have died. They failed to change the world while they were alive, and they sure can't do anything after they die.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: All I can do is listen to their grievances, do small rituals that won't change anything, make up for their regrets, and let them leave in peace.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It's the only reason for me to stay here.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: And that applies to you too.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Even if you put shackles and orders on me, I can't be of help.
You stand opposite each other. Her words are devoid of any emotion, but therefore devoid of any deception, and have an oddly convincing feel.
You open your mouth again when something suddenly slams into your back. A pair of arms wrap around your neck, and a girl's bright voice breaks the place's silence.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Don't overstay your welcome! It's clearly written on Oak Casket's door that she only does business with the dead.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Are you dead? Still alive? Then let's get out of here.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Follow me! I'm the best tour guide in Drifter Camp. Let me show you around!
You put up with Dudu and look over to Oak Casket. She's put on a gentle smile again.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I testify that Dudu is indeed the best tour guide here.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Are you leaving?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Please... give me a moment.
She takes the Bureau jacket from you and turns back inside. Shortly after, she returns to you with a cloak and drapes it over you.
It's a heavy cloak. You gently zip up the collar and recognize it as the style typical to Drifter Camp.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It's a great fit.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Your identity is somewhat sensitive, so be careful. People up there may recognize you.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Not everyone will see you as an enemy, but they won't see you as a friend either. Don't expose yourself so easily.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Thanks, but didn't you say that you wouldn't help me?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It's just a little reminder.
Oak Casket smiles. She takes out a pendant, hangs it around your neck, and gently places it on your chest.
At the bottom of the string hangs a small glass ball with a faint blue glow—It's the very Hypercube fragment you brought out of BR-004.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: ...You are carrying someone's trust. It's from someone noble, who spared nothing to send you back from the realm of the dead, and passed on the purest blessings and hopes to you.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: And you want to fulfill his last wish too?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Oh, that would be too hard. After all, you are not someone who values your life.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: We are all entrusted by the dead to walk this side of the world. I wish you well, too.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Hmph... You're really nice to him. What has he ever done to deserve this?
steps.female_content: Hmph... You're really nice to her. What has she ever done to deserve this?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Go for it, but don't force yourself. Let go of what you can't change.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: They stepped into the land of the dead just to bring you back alive.
The voices in front of you become somewhat distant, and the woman's expression is hard to read. She stops in front of the memorial, along with the many names of the deceased.
Like she's going to disappear into another world, like she'll never leave.
